$comment: THE CONTRACT LADDER — what each scenario is made of. GitHub issue #382, docs/33-difficulty-curve.md § 4.7, and packages/viz/src/shift/ladder.ts for the schema and the argument. Every field here is one of DC-R1's substrates: the crowd (demand, bounded by the building's own traffic profile), and the tower the contract hands the player (fabric — occupancy, and commissioning choices over the banks). THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO BAR, NO GOAL AND NO TIER IN THIS FILE: docs/33 § 4.3 and CLAUDE.md both forbid buying difficulty by moving the mark, and a field that does not exist cannot be authored. Every figure below was measured rather than chosen — the run is `CONTRACT_CURVE_SWEEP=1 CONTRACT_CURVE_SEEDS=50 CONTRACT_CURVE_OUT=<path> npx vitest run packages/viz/src/shift/contractCurve.sweep.test.ts` at seeds 20260824 + 7919n, day 1, dispatcher `collective`, and the table it produces is published in docs/33 § 4.7. `missRateTarget` is the DESIGN INTENT and never a measurement; three rows do not reach it and their notes say so with the probes attached. PROVENANCE, per the product owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed `data/` values: THESE FIGURES ARE AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, drafted for the owner to accept, tighten or reject. The distinction that ruling asks for is drawn field by field. What is MEASURED is each row's resulting miss rate, at the run and seeds named above. What is CHOSEN is the target each row aims at and which substrate is moved to reach it — that is game feel, not a measurement, and no amount of sweeping makes it one. So a reader disagreeing with a number here is disagreeing with a judgement, not correcting an error, and the lever is one field in this file rather than anything in code.
$growthComment: THE WEEK'S GROWTH, moved here from shift/types.ts#GROWTH_PER_DAY by DECISIONS.md § D1066 (wave AJ). A week's building on day d carries 1 + g × (d − 1) of its day-1 population, linearly (shift/growth.ts argues the linear form). defaultGrowthPerDay is the design's own 0.11 (design.html :1568) and applies wherever a rung declares no growthPerDay of its own: the career, Endless, a replay on a building with no rung, and every contract the week census has not re-derived. A rung's growthPerDay is RE-DERIVED BY A CENSUS, never chosen: shift/weekWay.sweep.test.ts measures each weekday against docs/33 DC-10 and data/week-way.json carries what it found, with the growth each row was measured under so a slope moved here without a re-run is refused as stale by shift/weekWay.test.ts. Bounded by shift/ladder.ts#GROWTH_PER_DAY_BOUNDS. No bar moves with it (shift/goals.ts#GOAL_BARS is pinned by goals.test.ts).

intent.note: NOT IN THE BAND, HANDED AS BUILT, AND THE REASON IS A CONFLICT RATHER THAN A GAP. The whole admissible envelope was measured and none of it reaches DC-4: 7 % is the residential profile's declared MAXIMUM, 1.95 is near this schema's own occupancy ceiling, and both cars at 0.5 m/s is the bottom of the hydraulic band — every combination of those reads 0 of 50. ONE car does reach the band, at 0.36 of 50 measured, AND IT IS REFUSED: a bank with one shaft has no assignment to make, so every shipped dispatcher produces the same run and the opening scenario would teach nothing about the thing the game is about. THE CROWD AND THE OCCUPANCY ARE ALSO NOT SHIPPED, and that is a second decision with its own reason: 7 % on a block let at 1.95 takes day 1 from 36 arrivals to 107 — which is exactly the volume ramp docs/33 § 1.6 asks the first hour to carry — and it moves NO verdict, 0.00 before and 0.00 after. A change that alters no figure the product publishes, while re-deriving every pinned figure taken on this building, is a change whose only support is a claim about how the first hour FEELS. The owner has scheduled a playtest for exactly that class of claim, so the figures are stated in docs/33 § 4.7 and the rung stays the identity until the playtest asks for them. The target is recorded so the debt stays visible.

Seven configurations were measured at 30 seeds and every one came back at 30 of 30: as built (queue misses 28, energy 10); occupancy 0.5 (energy 30); occupancy 1.15 with 18 cars (energy 30, queue 22); occupancy 1.0 with 21 cars (energy 30, queue 5); occupancy 1.3 with 22 cars (energy 30, queue 23); occupancy 1.6 with 21 cars (queue 30, energy 27); occupancy 2.0 with 32 cars (queue 30, energy 30). The two goals are OPPOSED on this tower: more cars empty the landings and raise the work per delivered leg, fewer cars do the reverse, and there is no fleet size at which both hold. That is docs/33 § 4.6's F7 re-measured on the fabric axis rather than on the threshold, it belongs to #234, and no arbitrary change is shipped here to look like an answer. The published figure is 1.00 of 50.

Day 1 reads 50 of 50 at docs/33 s 4.7d's budget and seeds, and so do c4 and c5 re-measured beside it, so five contracts are tied at the ceiling and the measurement has stopped ordering them. The goal doing the missing is the ENERGY BAR: shift/goals.ts asks for 80 kJ per delivered ride and a ride in this tower costs 105.9 kJ, measured under collective at 1 800 s. NO RUNG IN THIS FILE CAN MOVE THAT. Occupancy and rate are both DIVISORS of the crowd and the bar is a PER-LEG quantity: fewer riders means fewer legs and the same kilojoules on each, which is DECISIONS.md SS D468's own finding -- the bar is dominated by building fabric rather than by play -- restated at a fourth, fifth and sixth tower. docs/33 O2 and GitHub issue #234 own the remedy and it is a goal-set decision with an owner, not a ladder edit. THE TARGET IS RECORDED SO THE DEBT STAYS VISIBLE, exactly as c1's does for the opposite reason. The substrate is recorded as FABRIC because that is where the difficulty is -- the height of the tower and what a ride in it costs -- and NOT because this rung moves any fabric field: it moves nothing, and the identity is the whole of it.
